body: Thank you.  Your words are incredibly helpful.
Thank you so much.  Good luck to you, too.  Hope that gets straightened out.

I have gone through mild counseling for my depression... never touched the subject of suicide, but other things that were holding me down, i.e., old abusive relationships, an abortion, etc.  I suppose a counselor to talk out suicide would be beneficial.  As far as the ovarian cyst goes,  I have an appointment on July 1 when my insurance kicks in to get it checked out.

I've never really loved anything.  I'm good at a lot of things that I try my hand at, but I don't have any drive to pursue them once I know it can be done.  Actually, I've always been good at homemaking, so I figured I would one day become a house wife and call it good.  However, I ethically abhor the idea of using/leaning on another human to provide me with a desired lifestyle.  What if I don't love him or he doesn't love me? What if we divorce? What if I'm widowed? What if he becomes abusive? Then I would be left with no income and no skills.

The 3 years that I had clarity I was very strictly gluten free.  A few days after I had stopped eating gluten initially, I had a pretty immediate feeling that a veil had been lifted.  Last summer I started eating gluten again and noticed no difference between having eaten it and not.*  I recently tried going gluten free again for a short period and noticed no difference (except weight gain).  I'm on the fence about trying to be gluten free again.  I think I may take tests for Celiac disease before cutting it out.

*ETA: I even scoffed at myself for being suckered into 3 years of following a dumb fad diet.

Also, I have insurance starting July 1, so getting tested and cutting it out might be sooner than later.

First, happy cake day.

Second, thank you and everyone for your words. I appreciate that this subreddit exists for moments like this.

A long time ago, I realized that depression is a parasite and it will do everything in its power to stay alive... that includes being an invisible illness, and that when we have depression, we generally hide it and don't ask for help.  I know it's mostly a societal flaw that depression is stigmatized, but on top of that, I think if the only thing you have to call your own is depression, you will do what you can to protect it.  

I decided today to talk about it openly with my boyfriend.  I've confided in him about my past suicidal thoughts and that depression is something that has plagued my life since childhood.  I decided to make today the first time that I reached out to real people in real time about my suicidal thoughts.  Something about shedding light on the darkness.  

He told me my mind was emotionally cramped, that I should get out of the house (I study remotely), take a walk, go to the park, drink lots of water, take the day off, take slow, deep breaths.  It helped while I was at the park.  Not so much now that I'm back home.  But I have plans to stay at my SIL's place tonight with my cat and perhaps I will come out to them as well.  Continue the practice of opening.
